items.label: text
items.text: Safety Note: Direct heating of the acid is not recommended. Wear eye protection and do not evaporate the solution to dryness. The acid is best heated in a boiling tube placed in a water bath. Avoid contact with the crystals as they are harmful and irritating to both the skin and eyes.

items.label: section_header
items.text: MAKING SOLUBLE SALTS (EXCEPT SODIUM, POTASSIUM AND AMMONIUM SALTS)

items.label: text
items.text: These all involve reacting a solid with an acid. You can use any of the following mixtures:

items.label: list_item
items.text: acid + metal (but only for the moderately reactive metals from magnesium to iron in the reactivity series)

items.label: text
items.text: Whatever mixture you use, the method is basically the same.

items.label: text
items.text: The practical procedure for this is as follows:

items.label: list_item
items.text: Measure 50 cm³ of dilute sulfuric acid into a beaker and heat it on a tripod and gauze using a Bunsen burner.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Add a spatula full of black copper(ll) oxide and continue heating. If all the copper(ll) oxide disappears add more copper(ll) oxide until there is some left in the beaker. Stir the mixture well to make sure that no more will react. At this stage, we have added excess copper(Ill) oxide - there is more than enough to react with all the acid present. When there is copper(ll) oxide left, we know that all the acid has been neutralised.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Filter off the excess copper(ll) oxide and transfer the filtrate (solution), which is blue, to an evaporating basin. The solution we have now is copper(II) sulfate.

items.label: text
items.text: The equation for the formation of the solution is:

items.label: formula
items.text: C u O ( s ) + H _ { 2 } S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \rightarrow C u S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } O ( I )

items.label: list_item
items.text: Heat the solution of copper(ll) sulfate over a Bunsen burner to boil off some of the water and concentrate the solution.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Keep heating until a saturated solution is formed. We can test this by dipping a glass rod into the solution. If crystals form on the glass rod when we remove it we know that the solution is very close to saturated and crystals will also begin to form in the solution.
